title: two children in one turn of the parent
intent: The wave 44 of the plan of the owner: several children in one live turn of the parent.  The audit of wave 35 proved that several children in one turn work, but that proof was an audit of the code and not a claim of the map: nothing in the map was bound to it, and a green map said nothing about the delegation of the owner.  The wave binds the promise: a turn of the parent may hold two children, not one -- the model asks for a delegation twice in that turn, the journal of the parent holds the spawn of two children with different short ids, the turn of the parent goes on and does not wait for the children, and both children end on their own, later.  The check is offline (the parent asks for the delegations and the children answer after a delay) and the claim is bound to it.  The live check measures the same thing against a real provider: the model of the parent is asked for two delegations in one turn, and the journal of the parent is read afterwards.  Two defects of the live path were found and repaired while the check was written: the directories of the presets were bound with `let', and the tools of a child run in the event loop, long after the binding was gone -- the child was told that there is no agent named 'reviewer'; and the child had no tool `finish', so it could never end and worked for ever.
objection: The check of the wave is offline: the model of the parent is a fake, and it is the fake that asks for the two delegations.  The promise is that the KERNEL can hold two children in one turn, and the fake does not prove that a real model asks for two delegations in one turn -- the live check does that, and the live check lives outside the map (a provider is not a proof).  The live run of 23 November measured two spawns in one turn of the parent (sub-1 and sub-2, both at 10:28:04 UTC, in the turn turn-2), the finish of the parent after them (10:28:18) and the end of both children on their own; the first attempt of the same check failed for the two reasons named in the intent, and the failure of the child that could not end is the shape of the wave: a run that cannot end is a run that works for ever.  The wave does not touch the depth of the tree of the children (the grandchild is refused by the depth of the preset), does not make the children of a live turn parallel in the sense of the CPU, and does not prove that the children of a run survive a restart of the harness -- the tree in the journal is the claim of wave 37, and this wave only reads it.
refuted_by: the journal of the parent holds one spawn of a child where the model asked for two, or the two children carry the same short id, or a child is not alive when the turn of the parent is over, or a child does not end on its own, or the parent ends its turn between the two delegations, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: Measurements of 2026-11-23.  The check of the wave passes on the honest tree (2.0 s).  The control of the claim -- taken out of spec.json and applied to a copy of the tree: sed -i 's|(depth (1+ (yeah-delegate--depth-of session)))|(depth (+ 1 (yeah-delegate--depth-of session) (length (yeah-delegate--children-of session))))|' lib/yeah-delegate.el -- bites by the assertions of the check and not by a crash: 'the journal of the parent holds 1 spawn(s) of a child, not two: ("sub-1")' and 'the two children carry the short ids ("sub-1")' (code 1).  The control refuses the SECOND delegation: the first child is at the depth 1 and the second would be at the depth 2, and the preset allows the depth 1.  The control that was written first did not measure that: `1+' takes one argument, so the control broke every delegation with 'Wrong number of arguments: 1+, 2' -- a control that breaks the subject in another way is not a control, and it was measured before the claim was registered.  The live check passes (exit 0): the model of the parent was asked for two delegations in one turn against a real provider, the journal of the parent holds the spawn of two children with the short ids sub-1 and sub-2 (both at 10:28:04 UTC, in the turn turn-2), the finish of the parent came after them (10:28:18) and both children ended on their own (the child's own journal holds its own finish).  The gate of the project on this tree is GREEN: 184 claims of 184 hold, uncovered 0, and the run of the method executed 184 of 184 claims without being stopped.  The first attempt of the gate was killed (code 137) and the gate started it again by itself -- the gate waits for the run, it does not watch it.  The wave moved a line of lib/yeah-product.el (the session root of wave 109), and three pictures of the site named the old line: the picture of the layers, the picture of the placements and the guard of every picture.  They were re-anchored at the definitions they name (lib/yeah-product.el:264 and :166), the pictures of the site were rendered again, and the guard of the site says that the published picture is the picture of its source.
